ideas.rationale: I propose Huber iteratively reweighted least squares with residual MAD scaling and a positive scale floor. This standard approach limits large residual influence; improvement remains unmeasured. The supplied Huber reference concerns location estimation and does not establish regression performance.

I propose alternating between retaining the 80% smallest absolute residuals and refitting least squares. Hard residual selection is related to the thresholding theme in the supplied TRIP/BRHT abstract, without reproducing its prior or Bayesian machinery. The trimming fraction is a hypothesis requiring validation.

I propose Student-t residual reweighting with weights proportional to (degrees_of_freedom+1)/(degrees_of_freedom+(residual/scale)^2). This offers smooth downweighting distinct from Huber clipping and hard trimming. I make no novelty or measured performance claim; the supplied two-paper feed cannot establish literature coverage.
